title: This startup is paying employees to post on LinkedIn—and solving its hiring problem
tldr: A startup pays staff to post on LinkedIn, turning employee-generated content into a recruiting engine. A concrete case study on EGC delivering measurable business outcomes.
angle: When you pay employees to post: does incentivized EGC stay authentic or become noise?

title: Employee- And User-Generated Content Are Winning Attention, Users For AI Products On X
tldr: EGC and UGC are outperforming polished brand content in driving attention and adoption for AI products on X. Direct evidence that human-made content beats corporate polish.
angle: Why AI products lean on human, imperfect content to win trust in an AI-saturated feed.

title: Decision paralysis, lost conviction and no juniors: what brand creative leaders say AI is exposing
tldr: A MikeTeevee report finds AI is surfacing pre-existing organizational problems—eroded conviction, no junior pipeline—inside big in-house brand teams. A candid leadership read on AI's human costs.
why_fresh: new report on AI's org impact
angle: AI isn't creating new problems in content teams—it's exposing the ones we ignored.

title: Comscore data shows how AI discovery is splintering beyond ChatGPT
tldr: New Comscore data shows ChatGPT losing ground to Gemini and Claude, with AI citations becoming a key visibility metric for publishers and brands. A shift in how audiences discover content.
angle: AI visibility is now a multi-engine game—what content strategists must track beyond ChatGPT.

title: Some creators want to negotiate deals like TV networks
tldr: Creators, newly folded into traditional upfronts, now want their own upfront-style deals—signaling their maturation into media businesses. A structural shift in the creator economy.
angle: When creators negotiate like networks: the professionalization of the creator economy.

title: How Semafor is redefining the head of video role
tldr: Semafor's head of video sits between the newsroom and commercial team, reporting to the editor-in-chief with a dotted line to revenue—a new model for video-first publishing. A structural editorial-ops insight.
angle: The hybrid video role that breaks the wall between newsroom and revenue.

title: The word Steve Jobs wouldn’t let us say—and how it built Apple’s most loyal customers
tldr: An ex-Apple insider argues 'love'—not features—built Apple's loyal base, via how retail staff were trained to treat customers. A human-centered branding lesson with a concrete case.
angle: Human language over feature-speak: what internal vocabulary reveals about brand narrative.

title: Bots Don't Click—So What Will The Internet's New Business Model Be?
tldr: With AI agents replacing human clicks, the ad-and-traffic-funded web faces a reckoning over new monetization models. A big-picture shift in how content gets funded.
angle: When AI agents browse instead of humans, what happens to content business models?

title: Why Storytelling Is Brands’ Biggest E-Commerce Advantage
tldr: BoF argues narrative is the defensible edge for brands as commerce fragments across social and AI channels. Ties storytelling craft directly to conversion.
angle: Narrative as the last moat when discovery and purchase collapse into one moment.

title: 2026 employee advocacy stats to secure C-level buy-in
tldr: Sprout compiles fresh employee-advocacy data aimed at winning executive buy-in for EGC programs. Useful ammunition for pitching human-led amplification internally.
angle: The numbers that finally get leadership to fund employee advocacy.

title: Mark Ritson: The CMO role has shrunk. The extra letters are an attempt to regrow it
tldr: Ritson argues the proliferation of CMO title variants masks a diminished marketing function. A sharp take on executive positioning and comms leadership.
angle: Title inflation vs. real influence: what the shrinking CMO role means for comms leaders.

title: Templo’s visual identity for DeafCity Hub fuses creative coding, BSL and gestural motion capture
tldr: Templo built a purpose-driven identity centering Deaf culture using sign language and motion capture instead of the spoken word. A striking human-centered, inclusive design case study.
angle: Designing beyond the spoken word: what inclusive identity teaches about human-centered content.

title: Jenna Arts on why the stumbling, silly, ordinary human is the only one worth drawing
tldr: An illustrator makes the case for depicting flawed, ordinary humans over polished ideals. Aligns with the people-over-polish content ethos.
angle: The ordinary, imperfect human as the most magnetic subject in visual storytelling.

title: Founders Kept Buying Content That Sold Nothing. Pia Mikhael Built the Agency That Changed That.
tldr: An agency founder profile on why so much branded content fails to convert and how to fix the disconnect. A practical content-ROI angle for founders.
angle: Why most branded content sells nothing—and the operating fix behind content that does.

title: Two-thirds of Americans are gamers. Why hasn’t ad spending caught up?
tldr: At IAB PlayFronts, the industry probed why ad dollars lag behind gaming's massive audience. A media-consumption vs. spend mismatch worth watching.
angle: The gap between where audiences spend time and where brands spend money.
